core.title: Bind each journey spec to a user/system flow or journey declared by the plan artifacts
core.given: The plan artifacts declare at least one user/system flow or journey, and a journey spec exists (a file of the profile's e2e test kind actually selected by the stack's e2e test runner, or a test file whose header comments carry a user/system flow or journey binding marker per the profile's binding syntax)
core.when: the spec's binding is checked against the plan artifacts
core.then: The user/system flow or journey the spec binds to MUST be declared by the plan artifacts.
prefer: Bind to the declared subject the spec actually exercises: find the plan subject reached by its entrypoint and interactions; use that exact declared id in the spec's binding.
If the intended subject is absent from the plan, return to the authorized planning flow instead of inventing it in the tester repair.
avoid: Choosing any resolvable declared subject merely to clear the finding (false journey coverage).
Changing the binding to match a convenient test that proves another journey.
Declaring a new user/system flow or journey solely so an existing spec has something to bind.
unless: No plan (no user/system flows, no journeys): out of scope.
Vendored and generated trees (the profile's never-scanned roots) are not scanned.
Malformed bindings are reported by the companion binding-header rule, not here.
core.why: The binding traces an e2e test to the plan subject it exercises; no binding, two bindings, or an id the planning flow would reject is untraceable. Resolution is necessary but not sufficient: the bound subject must be the one the spec actually walks, and the plan changes only when product behavior requires it.
evidence: The binding id in the spec's binding resolves to a user/system flow or journey declared by the plan artifacts.
The end-to-end path actually walks the bound subject.
The final observable assertion proves that subject's user-facing behavior.
The plan was not changed only to give the spec something to bind.
verification: A journey spec is recognized two ways, so a misnamed one is still judged: a file of the profile's e2e name patterns that the stack's e2e test runner actually selects, or any test file whose header comments carry a user/system flow or journey binding marker per the profile's binding syntax. A test that merely mentions a journey URN in a string literal is not one.
Report specs with no binding, two bindings, or an id the planning flow would reject as untraceable; the check applies to all journey specs in the repository, existing or new.
Skip the profile's excluded vendored and generated roots; skip entirely when no user/system flows and no journeys are declared; leave malformed binding headers to the companion binding-header rule.

values: a plan artifact (under the plan root) declaring at least one user/system flow or journey
test file matching the profile's e2e name patterns (candidate journey spec by filename; filename alone is not sufficient)
test file of the profile's e2e kind actually selected by the stack's e2e test runner
test file whose header comments carry a user/system flow or journey binding marker per the profile's binding syntax
binding id does not resolve to a declared user/system flow or journey in the plan artifacts
the bound declared subject is not the subject the spec's end-to-end path actually walks

fires: The plan declares user-system-flows/journeys and an existing journey spec's binding names an id with no declaration in the plan artifacts.
A test file not matching the e2e name patterns whose binding header names an undeclared journey.
A journey spec has no binding, two bindings, or an id the planning flow would reject.
A spec's binding resolves to a declared subject but not the one its end-to-end path walks (prefer/avoid apply; the walked-subject obligation is owned by the companion split rule).
doesNotFire: The repository has no plan (no user/system flows, no journeys).
Files under the profile's excluded vendored and generated roots.
A unit test that merely mentions a journey URN inside a string.
A file matching the e2e name patterns but not selected by the e2e test runner and with no binding-marker header.
A malformed binding header (reported by the companion binding-header rule instead).

neutralityNotes: No new profile keys were needed: the plan root, e2e name patterns, test runner, user-system-flow/journey binding syntax and excluded roots all exist in the closed vocabulary. Realization-specific identifiers kept only in bunOnly: the validator id htmx_e2e_detector and the companion rule id tester.htmx.journey-binding-header; the core refers to companion rules generically. Sibling ids appearing in non-itemized fields (fires[3] and splitSuggestion naming tester.htmx.e2e-binding-matches-walked-subject and tester.htmx.plan-not-changed-to-rescue-spec) were likewise generalized in the core text; the split proposals themselves remain a Bun-sidecar concern, and their governing content is preserved in the core's prefer/avoid/why/evidence exactly as in bun.json.
